text:
Adam Fantilli told The Columbus Dispatch he's "not nervous at all" about his slow start, and he has reason to be calm about some of it. He's playing 20:21 a night on a Blue Jackets team that is winless in five, and his finishing is only a touch cold: five goals on 5.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances). The worry is the rest of the line. He has seven points in 19 games, 1.09 per 60 against a talent range we put around 2.0, and three points in his last 10 with 3.0 expected goals of his own.

The skills haven't gone anywhere. Last season Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.4 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area, 93rd percentile among forwards, and he carried the puck in on 58% of his entries. Speed bursts put him in the 87th percentile. The catch is the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on the ice than with almost any forward, and Columbus holds 45.5% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there. Watch whether his minutes hold; Tuesday on Long Island he played 13.
